# Results — Study 875 (Idiosyncratic-Vol Change)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: sort a
cross-section on the **change** in idiosyncratic (market-model residual) volatility — each
name's `recent-21d residual vol − prior-21d residual vol` — long the **falling-idio-vol**
names, short the **rising-idio-vol** names, betting a rising idio-vol (deteriorating
information environment / rising disagreement) precedes lower returns. Offline &
deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
Reported as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete calendar month; the partial current month is
dropped). Fingerprint `5384b8f7f128` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Market model | the market factor is the **equal-weight cross-sectional mean** daily return; each name's idio vol = std of its CAPM residual `r − a − b·mkt`, vectorised via `resid_var = var(r) − cov(r,mkt)²/var(mkt)` |
| Signal | **delta-IVOL** = `idio_vol(recent 21d) − idio_vol(prior 21d)` (two non-overlapping windows), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`); positive = idio-vol **rising**, negative = **falling** |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by delta-IVOL; **long the bottom 30%** (most falling), **short the top 30%** (most rising), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled falling-vs-rising books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a **level-vs-change additivity regression** against the idio-vol level puzzle (501); a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. The names
whose idio-vol ran hardest before they were delisted / de-rated are exactly the ones absent
from a survivor panel.

## The headline — long-falling-idio-vol / short-rising-idio-vol spread

Daily equal-weight bottom-30% minus top-30% delta-IVOL spread (n = **4,104** days):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long falling-idio-vol − short rising-idio-vol)** | **+0.87 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **+0.86** |
| one-sample *t* | +0.85 |
| falling-idio-vol book / rising-idio-vol book | +8.43 bps / +7.56 bps (Welch *t* = +0.33) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | +0.21 |

The spread has the **claimed sign** (falling-idio-vol names very slightly out-earn
rising-idio-vol names) but is **statistically indistinguishable from zero** — NW *t* =
**+0.86**, well below the |t| ≥ 2 bar. The *change* in idiosyncratic vol carries essentially
no reliable cross-sectional return information on 50 liquid US mega-caps.

## Placebo — is the (tiny) tilt a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the delta-IVOL sort but read each day's forward returns from a **column-permuted** panel
(signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **+0.87 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | −0.014 bps (0.886) |
| position of observed | ≈ **+0.99σ** above the placebo mean (right-tail p = **0.165**) |

The observed spread sits barely one sigma into the right tail — comfortably inside what the
permutation null produces by chance. Not distinguishable from noise.

## Additivity — is the idio-vol CHANGE anything beyond the idio-vol LEVEL (501)?

The whole point of the study is to separate the idio-vol *change* from the idio-vol *level*
puzzle. We build the idio-vol **level** sort (long low residual vol, short high residual vol)
on the same tape, then regress the change spread on the level spread and read the residual
(Newey-West) *t*:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| idio-vol **level** spread (501-style) | **−3.85 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−2.85**) |
| corr(change spread, level spread) | +0.216 |
| change spread β on level spread | +0.158 |
| **change alpha net of level** | **+1.47 bps/day** (NW *t* = **+1.52**) |

Two honest readings. First, the idio-vol *level* puzzle itself **inverts** on this mega-cap
survivor tape (−3.85 bps/day, NW *t* = −2.85: high-idio-vol mega-caps *out-earned* low-idio-vol
ones over 2010–2026, the familiar tech-momentum sign-flip, echoing study 501's mega-cap
result). Second, the change and level spreads are only weakly correlated (corr +0.216), so the
delta-IVOL is a *largely distinct* axis — but its alpha net of the level effect is only
**+1.47 bps/day (NW *t* = +1.52)**, not significant. The change is near-orthogonal to the
level, and **equally empty**: nothing additive survives.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,970) | +2.86 bps | **+2.31** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −0.98 bps | −0.63 |

**The signal does not hold across eras.** It is significant with the claimed sign in the
first half (NW *t* = +2.31) but vanishes and *flips sign* in the second (−0.98 bps, *t* =
−0.63). A full-sample *t* of +0.86 that is carried entirely by one era and reverses in the
other is exactly the fragile, non-stationary pattern the desk stamps **None** — one era is not
a signal.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | +0.87 bps | 2.14 bps | **−1.27 bps** | −1.25 | −0.31 | −3.2%/yr |
| **5 bps** | +0.87 bps | 10.14 bps | **−9.27 bps** | −9.12 | −2.26 | −23.4%/yr |

The +0.87 bps/day gross edge is smaller than the **2.14 bps/day** round-trip friction at a
mere 1 bp one-way, so the book is already **net negative** at the lowest realistic cost and
bleeds badly at 5 bps. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel: a common market factor plus, per name, a persistent latent
idio-vol tilt that modulates its residual-vol amplitude and (with `edge>0`) depresses its
forward mean when idio-vol is rising. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.16** (sd 0.95), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 1/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.002`, seed 875) | **+8.43** (Welch *t* = +4.15) |

The detector recovers a *planted* rising-idio-vol-derates relation cleanly and fires on
**1/20** nulls — the nominal 5% type-I rate, i.e. unbiased — so the flat real-tape result is a
genuine absence of edge, not a broken sort. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never
cited in support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The *change* in idiosyncratic vol — distinct from the idio-vol level
  puzzle (corr with the level spread is only +0.216) — carries **no** reliable cross-sectional
  return signal on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The long-falling / short-rising spread is **+0.87
  bps/day** (NW *t* = **+0.86**): the *claimed* sign, but statistically zero, sitting only
  +0.99σ into a 1,000-permutation placebo (p = 0.17), and — decisively — **not robust across
  eras** (significant +2.31 in 2010–2017, then −0.63 and sign-flipped in 2018–2026). It adds
  just +1.47 bps/day (*t* = +1.52) on top of the (itself inverted) level effect. A clean
  20-seed synthetic control confirms the machinery is unbiased, so the flat result is real.
  The change is **not additive** — near-orthogonal to the level and equally empty.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The +0.87 bps/day gross edge is smaller than the 2.14 bps/day
  round-trip friction at 1 bp one-way; the book is net **−1.27 bps/day** at 1 bp and
  **−9.27 bps/day** at 5 bps. Nothing to trade.
